events.credibility_reason: math.GM preprint read only via abstract and a search summary; the summary reports the proposition takes Goldbach and twin prime conjectures as given, and that is in tension with the abstract.

Claims infinitely many both-twin sums, which implies the twin prime conjecture; the same author claims a twin prime proof via complexity theory, a method the problem is not known to yield to; no uptake in ~6.7 years on a would-be landmark; non-refereed venue; never read.
Claimed proof of the twin prime conjecture via complexity-class equivalences; no expert uptake in over five years on a landmark claim; method far from the field; non-refereed venue.

why: The statement is universal over all even n > 4208. Every computational event (Zwillinger to 10^6, Noe to 10^9, Pandey to 10^11 in both the OEIS comment and the arXiv paper) checks finitely many instances, so each is scored instances (F5). The researcher's alternative reading, that the exceptional set is a quantity the statement names, does not hold: the statement asserts the set is contained in [0, 4208], and no finite census moves that assertion. Pandey's theorem and its 10^14 run concern the weaker statement (S), and the theorem is conditional, so neither adds anything beyond instances. Pandey's least-witness representation is just one instance, not an object bearing on the statement. Dubner's proposal is the statement itself, so it is none. The formal-conjectures entry formalises the statement only, so it is none. Its unnamed AI agent drafted the issue text and did no mathematics, so its AI role is none. Vega's claims target the twin prime conjecture or an infinitude variant, and they carry several F10 signals together, so they are not_credible as well as variant. Dubner 2005 and the two bounded-gap results are neighbouring problems, so variant. Their AI attributions are irrelevant here and have no authors' quote behind them.
doubts: Zwillinger's 'digested' rests on publication in Math. Comp. per a catalogue summary. It is immaterial, because the event is discarded as instances.
